case: The same four natural-key create-path rows, in reverse order.
why: Every check over this table is a per-row comparison against the registry and against the command, plus a set comparison of the record names. The order the rows are written in changes no record identity and no create path. A control that refuses a harmless reordering is one contributors learn to route around.

value.why: 08 section 1 names a writer-key assignment as (field_path, epoch). Two records for one field path in one epoch are two answers to who may write this field -- and the whole of the F6D-05 repair reads that answer.
One decision per obligation per window. A second row is two answers to whether the obligation was performed or breached, which is the question the record exists to have exactly one answer to.

05 section 6 answers the tenth (d)-class example of the protocol by having a second claimant JOIN the first and inherit its outcome. That answer is unreachable unless the create path resolves: two rows for one triple is a race and a second release.

05 section 2 gives the identity as origin plus arrival sequence, and the per-origin subcap that guard.intake.per_origin_subcap_preserves_intake protects is counted over exactly this key. A create path that made a second admission for one arrival would miscount the cap it is the subject of.
